why: Untargeted sequencing of sewage and airport wastewater to catch unknown pathogens is already being piloted, by the Nucleic Acid Observatory and in the CDC's traveller genomic surveillance; an in-line box is packaging, not a new capability.
found: Nucleic Acid Observatory runs pathogen-agnostic wastewater metagenomic sequencing pilots; CDC Traveler-based Genomic Surveillance sequences airport wastewater.

why: Automatic air samplers that identify listed germs already exist for biothreat defence (Smiths BioFlash), so the new part is the price and place: a filter-free, smoke-detector-cost unit in every classroom and ward; is that 10x enough? My pick: keep.
found: Military and transit biothreat air monitors (e.g. Smiths Detection BioFlash) collect air and identify listed agents automatically; nothing cheap enough for every room.

why: Printing shelf-stable vaccine patches at the outbreak from a sequence sent over the network removes both the factory and the cold chain; the MIT printer is still preclinical.
found: MIT tabletop microneedle vaccine printer (Nature Biotechnology 2024), preclinical; factory-made microneedle patches (Vaxxas, Micron Biomedical) in human trials.

why: A vaccine stockpiled against a whole virus family before the outbreak turns months of lead time into zero; mosaic nanoparticles protect animals against relatives not in the vaccine, but none is approved.
found: Caltech mosaic-8 and mosaic-7COM nanoparticle vaccines in animal studies and early trials; CEPI funds broadly protective coronavirus vaccines. None licensed.
